sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 5, L NS. Every factor has its own supporting evidence, counter-fact, rationale and evidence IDs in the attached audit. GQS means Growth Quality, not governance quality.

Exact Decimal calculations: BQS known weighted contribution 4.16, observed weight 0.80, missing CAP/BAL weight 0.20; mathematical completion bounds 4.36–6.16, no point score. GQS known contribution 5.55, observed weight 0.85, missing CAP 0.15; bounds 5.70–7.05, no point score. IAS known contribution 1.10, observed weight 0.30, missing Q/R/L 0.70; generic bounds 1.80–8.10. Propagating the BQS bounds tightens IAS mathematical bounds to 2.64–7.14, still not a score or confidence interval. Full weights and each contribution are embedded; no renormalization or average of known factors.

No governance ≤3 override applies to GOV4; no persistent-cash ≤3 cap is imposed on CASH4; G3 is Hold, not verified Fail. Missing BQS passes through to Q as NS. No ranking flag is true. CAP missing independently blocks quality/growth point scores, while the financial-reliability hold is separately material. Price is not used to inflate business-quality factors. Positive cash below the required operating buffer still fails funding. Even buffer-compliant scenarios require current-resource verification: R stays NS.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Gallard designs/manufactures engineered steel, ductile and grey-iron castings and machined components, with exposure to railway products and smaller industrial applications. This is not a commodity TMT-bar or flat-steel rolling company. Sleeploop is wholly owned and operates rebonded foam and machining; its purchase in February 2024 changes the consolidated comparison base. Parent/subsidiary sales and machining charges must be eliminated rather than added as a second revenue stream.

FY25 railway revenue was ₹41.0769 crore, 77.04% of group sales; rebonded foam ₹10.4926 crore, 19.68%. H1 FY26 railway share was 78.88% and foam 16.05%. Defence was only ₹0.0207 crore, 0.04%, in FY25, so a defence-led valuation story is presently unsupported by revenue mix. Production is concentrated at leased industrial premises around Pithampur; domestic railway/customer procurement dominates the disclosed thesis, and no material export-growth claim is underwritten here.

Economics depend on casting yield, metal/energy costs, machining content, qualification, rejection rates and customer collections. Orders do not create cash automatically. Top ten customers represented 87.48% of FY25 revenue; largest 18.35%, top three roughly 49%. H1 FY26 top ten remained 84.74%. Purchase orders are not guaranteed multi-year volumes. Foundry capacity was 2,400 tonnes, machining 7,500 units and foam 3,150 units; FY25 utilization was 92.94%, 88.32% and 40.41%, respectively. The units are different and cannot be added as if all were tonnes.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The best moat argument is qualification and process know-how: engineering acceptance, tooling, consistent casting quality and machining integration can make a qualified supplier harder to replace than an undifferentiated trader. Rising utilization and disclosed margins support a useful position. They do not establish protected market share, contractual pricing power or a long-lived economic moat. Customer concentration makes customer power substantial; delayed approvals, rejects, tender competition and raw-material/power costs can reverse reported margins.

Three comparison lenses are used. Nitin Castings is a listed casting comparator: the issuer prospectus's FY25 snapshot shows ₹150.5738 crore revenue, ₹15.3635 crore EBITDA and 10.20% margin. Pritika Engineering is a casting/machining comparator with ₹117.3836 crore revenue, ₹18.2668 crore EBITDA and 15.56% margin in that same table. Simplex Castings is a broader engineering-castings/machining competitor serving industrial and rail-related applications; it is a qualitative capabilities check, not a precisely matched margin or valuation peer. The undated official profile is not used to assert a cutoff-date numerical advantage.

Gallard's higher apparent operating margin cannot by itself prove superiority: product mix, foam consolidation, subsidy treatment, conversion costs and customer contracts differ. No current comparable EV multiple, peer ranking or sector-average premium is manufactured from stale snapshot data. MOAT5 reflects contestable qualification/customer relationships. Upgrade would require verified retention, repeat competitive wins, rejection/yield trends and durable cash returns; downgrade would follow loss of qualified status or sustained price concessions.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue history in crore: FY22 ₹14.0955; FY23 ₹20.5906; FY24 ₹26.8244; FY25 ₹53.3180; FY26 ₹68.0449. Annual additions are ₹6.4951, ₹6.2338, ₹26.4936 and ₹14.7269 crore. The FY23–FY26 reported CAGR is 48.95%; four-year FY22–FY26 48.23% is a reported mixed-perimeter diagnostic, not organic growth. FY24 includes only post-acquisition Sleeploop; FY25 is the first full-year group base. A five-year comparable consolidated CAGR and ten-year CAGR are NS, not zero.

Window selection preceded scoring: use three-year same-parent expansion because a five-year like-for-like group/organic series is unavailable. Remove disclosed parent sales to the subsidiary at both endpoints: FY23 ₹20.5906 − ₹0.5965 = ₹19.9941 crore; FY26 ₹57.4722 − ₹0.4132 = ₹57.0590 crore, 41.84% CAGR. Parent raw FY26 growth is 34.88%. The cross-check reduces acquisition accounting distortion but does not isolate pricing, volume, acquired machining benefits or product mix. Original FY22 statements give FY21 parent revenue ₹9.082537 crore, in thousand-rupee source units; the resulting five-year parent context is separately labeled, not spliced into group figures. Original FY22 ₹14.097339 differs slightly from later restated ₹14.0955.

Latest primary results show H1 FY26 ₹31.5602 crore and H2 ₹36.4847, with latest H2 FY25 ₹32.1062: H2 growth 13.64%. The latest FY25 annual total implies H1 ₹21.2118, unlike the older DRHP ₹24.4730; the ₹3.2612 crore interim regrouping is not reconciled. Mechanical implied H1 growth must not be sold as a clean organic acceleration. No single-half-year scoring upgrade is applied. REV starting anchor 9 for ≥30% is limited to 8 by medium evidence confidence; no extra arbitrary small-base deduction or TAM-based upgrade.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand access is tangible but concentrated: existing rail qualifications and management-reported five locomotive-bogie prototype approvals provide a route to higher-value work. Bulk approval was expected after field trials within twelve months; approval, order receipt, delivery and collection are separate milestones. Couplings and brake-disc opportunities are not assumed to be already producing sales. Foundry production progressed from 1,270 tonnes in FY23 to 1,525 in FY24 and 2,230.55 in FY25; H1 FY26 1,150 against half-year capacity 1,200 leaves little existing foundry headroom.

The IPO expansion plan targets 6,100 foundry tonnes and 10,000 machining units. Project cost was approximately ₹21.699 crore, including ₹0.9689 already incurred, leaving IPO object ₹20.7301; existing land was sufficient for this project. The later ₹7.5 crore land proposal is therefore an additional capital decision, not automatically the same object. No completed commissioning certificate or new-plant utilization proof is available at cutoff. The annual scenarios explicitly pay remaining project cost, additional land, maintenance and further growth capex, and fund operating working capital. Terminal capacity diagnostics compare implied blended parent revenue per produced tonne with FY25; this is not a quoted selling price or proof that capacity is ready.

CAP is NS. The model contains both financing-side book capital and operating-capital builds including CWIP, intangible assets, goodwill, capital advances and deposits. Positive ΔNOPAT/Δcapital ratios are not attributable incremental investment returns. Tax liabilities, subsidy asset reductions and an unreconciled ₹0.9131 crore capital-advance movement are exposed, not plugged. A 12–16% nominal post-tax capital-cost diagnostic is justified as a broad SME operating-risk range, not a measured WACC; the separate equity hurdle remains 15%. Unit/cohort cash returns above that range need to be demonstrated. GQS remains NS, 85% factor coverage, rather than awarding a high runway score for planned capacity alone.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held 67.16% at March 2026. The fresh IPO created 2.5 million new shares, lifting issued capital from 7.0 million to 9.5 million; this is real 35.71% share-count dilution, unlike an earlier bonus split. A disclosed pre-IPO transfer of 280,000 promoter shares at ₹105 generated ₹2.94 crore for sellers, not the company. A lower pre-IPO transaction price than ₹150 IPO price deserves context, but alone does not establish unfair dealing.

The prospectus admits historical Section 185 connected-loan contraventions of approximately ₹0.48197 crore across earlier periods. A compounding application was filed on 25 July 2025; disclosed company exposure was ₹0.10–0.50 crore and a hearing was scheduled for 1 December 2025. No final disposal order was verified. Do not convert a procedural exposure into a proven fine, add individual penalties to company debt, or double-count the ₹0.40 crore contingent claim if overlapping. Audit reports did not identify lender default or fraud, while the audit-trail software functionality was absent. G1 is Conditional, not an unsupported finding of fraud or severe minority abuse.

The statutory auditor resigned on 8 September 2026 after fee/scope agreement failed. Its annexure says no information was withheld and no other material reason existed. A replacement was proposed for the September AGM; board proposal is not independently verified completion of every subsequent filing. Parent purchases of Sleeploop services ₹7.4313 crore eliminate on consolidation. Abarro purchases ₹0.2766 crore and a proposed related COO pay increase from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh monthly merit related-party approval and market-pay checks. Total management employee remuneration and selected RPT-note coverage should not be conflated.

Promises versus delivery: FY23–FY25 foundry output/utilization growth is delivered; November 2025 fundraising is delivered; March 2026 remaining expansion use is ₹16.2226 crore and debt object ₹7.2 crore entirely unused then; new capacity commissioning is unverified, not automatically overdue; June additional land remains a proposal/LOI with ₹7.5 versus ₹7.02 crore cost difference; bulk prototype approval is pending evidence rather than booked orders. EXEC5 gives credit for operating delivery but no automatic credit for all capital announcements.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The embedded five-year model contains reported revenue, earnings, CFO, investing capex, balance-sheet components, average-capital ROE/ROCE/ROIC proxies and explicit source scope. FY26 operating EBIT is ₹12.1909 PBT + ₹1.5001 finance − ₹1.7543 other income = ₹11.9367 crore. Add ₹3.3010 depreciation to obtain ₹15.2377 EBITDA, 22.39% margin. Common-tax normalized PAT is (₹11.9367 − ₹1.5001) × 75% = ₹7.82745 crore, versus reported ₹9.1048. The ₹1.4454 subsidy income is removed once; the ₹3.6577 capital-grant cash receipt is investing, not CFO. Asset/grant depreciation adjustments mean normalized income is analytical, not an audit restatement. No consistent gross-profit line is disclosed; materials value added is not mislabeled gross profit.

FY26 CFO ₹4.1881 crore / PAT ₹9.1048 = 46.00%. FY24–FY26 latest-comparative ratio of sums is 67.78%, not an average of annual ratios; using prospectus FY25 CFO gives 53.89%. Finance is classified below CFO, so after-finance-cost proxy is only 44.68%. PPE/CWIP/intangible cash purchases ₹11.3721 give FCF −₹7.1840; adding capital-advance cash outflow ₹2.3930 gives −₹9.5770. Multi-year reported FCF proxy totals −₹16.1980. Capex explains FCF, not weak CFO. FY25 cash-flow reclassification increases CFO ₹2.5513, decreases CFI ₹0.5364 and CFF ₹2.0149, leaving net movement unchanged; full explanation is unresolved. The prospectus cash-flow starting PBT is ₹8.4087 crore versus ₹8.4210 in its P&L, a further ₹0.0123 crore discrepancy; latest annual cash flow instead starts before the separate exceptional item at ₹8.4024. FY25 other income ₹0.1874 plus separate exceptional subsidy ₹0.0186 equals prospectus ₹0.2060, so normalization excludes both once.

Receivables ₹19.9930 crore rose 35.08%, faster than 27.62% sales; balances beyond six months ₹0.9917 include ₹0.5259 at two-to-three years. Inventory ₹6.8726 and trade payables ₹6.1355 enter working capital. Reduction in supplier financing absorbs cash. Debt ₹21.1575 includes ₹2.5327 current maturities, ₹9.0858 demand loans and director funding; do not add these again. Legacy current-tax/statutory provision ₹1.8654, CSR ₹0.0765 and gratuity ₹0.0653 are explicit model claims, outside operating WC. Guarantees ₹0.8842 are not all funded debt; contingent claim ₹0.40 is modeled with overlap caveat.

Cash/current bank ₹26.4124 includes ₹26.125 deposits and only ₹0.2874 cash/current accounts; noncurrent deposits ₹3.6111 cannot be assumed free. IPO schedule ₹26.015 is contained within reported deposits, never added again. Maturity-caption overlap and current use require confirmation. Paid IPO expenses ₹4.9088 are already in March cash; securities-premium deduction ₹4.959 differs ₹0.0502, unresolved, not deducted a second time. Capital-advance balance change ₹3.3061 versus cash ₹2.3930 leaves ₹0.9131 unexplained. Operating-invested-capital reconciliation residuals ₹2.1604 FY25 and ₹1.9373 FY26 remain visible. The current 9.5m-share denominator gives reported EPS ₹9.584 versus historical weighted EPS ₹11.59; normalized current-share EPS ₹8.2394. No subsidiary investment or operating property is added to enterprise value a second time.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹159.95 and 9.5 million shares, equity value is ₹151.9525 crore. P/E using FY26 profit/current shares is 16.69, not the misleading 13.80 obtained from weighted historical EPS; normalized P/E is 19.41. Verified current EV is null. Historical March-claim/October-price diagnostics bracket cash treatment, but unutilized IPO funds are not freely excess cash and are not worthless either. Preferred method is annual operating earnings/EV with explicit claims and funding; a nine-case counterfactual FCFF DCF cross-check normalizes terminal reinvestment at assumed 15% ROIC. It remains a pre-funding enterprise-valuation diagnostic, with conditional usable value and return fields null because its unrescued base is below the required cash floor. It is not a validated WACC/project-return valuation.

Every October-to-October case embeds five annual rows for revenue, EBITDA, depreciation, EBIT, tax, interest, operating WC, CFO, maintenance/project/land/growth capex, earmark draws, debt principal, legacy claims, fees, free cash and shares. March audited resources are held unchanged at October solely as an explicit hypothetical opening assumption: ₹0.2874 free cash, ₹26.015 earmarked IPO pool and ₹21.1575 debt. Current demand-facility rollover is unverified; no new bank-debt plug exists. Earmarks release only against assigned ₹16.2226 project, ₹7.2 debt and ₹2.5924 GCP costs. Existing IPO fees are not charged again. Year-one legacy tax ₹1.8654 and CSR ₹0.0765 plus scenario legal calls are paid separately from future earnings tax; an illustrative ₹0.117951 early-repayment fee applies the prospectus 3% SIDBI rate to its then ₹3.9317 outstanding, not a claimed current lender quote.

Base sales growth is 20/18/16/14/12%, EBITDA margins 21/21.5/22/22/22%, ONWC 30% of sales and terminal EV 8× EBITDA. Bull growth 30/28/25/22/18%, margins 23–24%, ONWC 27%, terminal 10×, with higher maintenance and growth capex. Bear has −12/4/6/6/5% growth, 15–17% margins, 42% ONWC, accelerated land/project calls and terminal 6×. In each case operating property, goodwill and subsidiary earnings are already in operating value, never an additional asset credit. Remaining earmarked cash is not terminal surplus; debt and gratuity are deducted once. Base minimum free cash ₹0.7395 crore breaches the required ₹1 crore annual operating floor by ₹0.2605366 crore in year one. Its ordinary and conditional returns/entry fields are null, not made fundable merely because cash is positive. A separate base-buffer equity rescue at ₹111.965 per new share and 5% costs raises ₹0.2742491 crore gross, increases share count 0.2578%, and yields a conditional 12.30% five-year CAGR and ₹142.06 hurdle-price diagnostic. These are not a buy zone or committed funding. All ordinary returns, terminal prices, entry prices and current DCF value fields remain null, including the funded hypothetical bull and rescue cases, because current resources/reliability are unverified. Bear also fails in year one and has no conditional return. Annual closing-floor compliance does not establish intrayear cash availability; that remains an explicit limitation.

The model contains 27 full growth/margin/exit-multiple combinations, three obligation/capex sensitivities, 12/15/18% hurdle diagnostics, entry/exit execution-cost sensitivities and fee-dependent rescue cases. Reverse 15%, 5× and 10× solves retain annual funding; a solved terminal price with an interim deficit is not feasible. No probability-weighted ordinary expected return or R score is inferred from conditional cases.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that reported growth is monetizing neither qualification nor returns fast enough: concentrated rail customers can defer orders and collections just as new capacity, land and working-capital cash calls arrive. Existing high utilization may reflect a small base rather than a scalable moat. Foam can dilute the rail narrative, and grant income plus equity-financed expansion can make headline profits and cash look stronger than recurring per-share cash economics.

A linked severe stress combines 25% first-year revenue decline, flat second year, 10–16% margins, ONWC at 50% of sales, upfront land/project expenditure and partial demand-loan repayment. The genuine unfunded path fails in year one and reaches a ₹18.5662 crore deficit. Every ordinary and conditional return is null; later rows are expressly counterfactual continuation diagnostics, not survival forecasts. Specialized equipment/leasehold property is not valued at book value as guaranteed liquidation protection. Lack of liquidity can compound economic loss and cannot be solved by a market-maker label.

A separate hypothetical rescue raises equity at 70% of the entry quote, ₹111.965, with 5% gross issue costs and enough net cash to restore a ₹1 crore annual buffer. It requires ₹20.5960 crore gross and increases shares by 19.36%; existing-holder ownership falls by a different, explicitly calculable fraction. Fee sensitivities 0% and 10% are modeled, not free equity assumed. Financing is not committed. This is not evidence that actual default exists; it demonstrates material dilution dependence. Thesis break: failure to collect large customer balances while full capital commitments/loan calls crystallize without verified cash or sanctioned funding.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five times the entry price in five years requires 37.97% annual shareholder return; ten times requires 58.49%, before friction. A large addressable railway market is not a mechanism for either. The reverse model fixes base operating margins, working-capital needs, annual maintenance/project/land/growth investment and 8× exit EBITDA, then solves constant sales growth while retaining every cash and claim row. The 15% reverse hurdle requires 19.09% constant revenue growth; 5× requires 44.25% and 10× 66.30%. All three unrescued reverse solutions breach the operating cash floor in year one. The extreme targets force rapid scale and produce first-year funding failure in the unrescued solution; therefore ordinary and conditional investment returns remain null even though the terminal price equation can be solved.

The bottom-up constraint is capacity and collection: 6,100 foundry tonnes is only a plan; 85% terminal utilization and an assumed 84% parent external-revenue mix yield an implied revenue-per-tonne diagnostic, not a current order book. Higher product value, additional machinery, rejects, energy, skills and customer approvals must all support that scale. Any rescue must dilute existing owners and pay issue costs; repeated capital raises cannot be assumed neutral. No terminal multiple expansion is allowed to hide inadequate operating growth. A 5× or 10× outcome is a speculative tail requiring evidence well beyond the present record, not the base thesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Cash and IPO bridge: baseline 31 March free cash/current accounts ₹0.2874 crore and earmarks ₹26.015. Obtain monthly bank/encumbrance and utilization reconciliations through October before any ordinary-return underwriting; unexplained overlap remains a gate hold.
2. Debt and repayment: baseline ₹21.1575 crore, including ₹9.0858 demand borrowing and ₹2.5327 maturities; verify actual ₹7.2 IPO debt repayment, charges and renewed limits. A material due repayment without available funds is a G3 failure trigger, not merely a weak ratio.
3. Receivable conversion: baseline ₹19.993 crore, ₹0.9917 older than six months, FY26 CFO/PAT 46%. Require customer-level collections and sustained rolling CFO/PAT above 80% as an upgrade indicator; continued sub-50% conversion or aging growth is a warning, not an automatic fraud claim.
4. Commissioned capacity: baseline 2,400 foundry tonnes and FY25 92.94% use; verify physical commissioning, customer acceptance, utilization and remaining cost for the 6,100 plan. Cost overrun >20% or unexplained milestone delay reopens EXEC/funding.
5. Project returns: reconcile ₹0.9131 capital-advance discrepancy and capital cohorts; track cash operating return after tax against a reasoned 12–16% capital-cost range. No CAP upgrade from book ROCE alone.
6. Customer/product mix: baseline top ten 87.48%, largest 18.35% FY25. Track top-customer order renewal, rail approvals, rejects and price realization; loss of a major relationship or >20% sales decline challenges runway.
7. Governance controls: obtain final Section 185 compounding order, new auditor acceptance/AGM outcome, audit-trail activation and related-party remuneration approvals. New substantiated deliberate minority harm would change G1/GOV, not be offset by cheapness.
8. Land and commitments: reconcile ₹7.5 proposal versus ₹7.02 LOI, paid versus unpaid cost, taxes/infrastructure and distinction from IPO expansion. Do not capitalize the same cash call twice.
9. Per-share earnings: use current fully diluted shares, exclude nonrecurring grant/other income once, verify further issues/convertibles and compare normalized EPS and cash per share, not weighted EPS alone.
10. Trading: obtain complete primary 60/20-session BSE volumes, actual traded values, spreads/depth and circuit-lock observations. Recalculate 1,000-share lot floor/ceiling and realistic whole-lot participation before assigning L. Missing observations remain unknown.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification is Hold — unresolved / research watchlist for a capacity-led industrial-growth thesis. This is a research action category, not advice to hold or purchase an existing personal position. It does not qualify as an established compounder: durable moat, attributable incremental returns, resilient funded growth and reliable per-share cash progression are not demonstrated together. It is not declared an Avoid for proven severe governance abuse, because that standard is not met by the available evidence; G2/G3/G4 holds still prevent favorable actionable classification.

No quality, growth-quality or investment point ranking is permitted while their material factors are NS. A lower price alone cannot clear accounting, current-funding or execution gates. The unrescued base has no hurdle entry. The separate base-buffer-rescue ₹142.06 conditional diagnostic is not an entry recommendation because it assumes discounted new equity, fees and unverified current resources. Reopening requires reconciled audited/current cash-flow and deposit bridges, sanctioned funding and paid/unpaid capital commitments, successful commissioning/collections and primary lot-level execution data. Only then can R, BAL and L be scored and an ordinary price-dependent conclusion considered. No trade is part of this research deliverable.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source hierarchy is explicit: final November 2025 prospectus for detailed restated FY23–FY25, March 2025 DRHP only for earlier FY22 and the preserved interim-comparative discrepancy, FY26 audited annual for latest numbers/notes, primary results for the latest half-year table, and issuer disclosures for IPO use, land, governance and auditor resignation. Original FY22 P&L was visually inspected to validate the thousand-rupee FY21 revenue context. Official interoperable master establishes exact security identity/lot/share count; secondary completed OHLCV is limited to quote and incomplete execution diagnostics. No later information beyond 20 October is admitted merely because retrieval occurred on 21 October. Undated peer profile supports only a qualitative capabilities lens.

Every source carries URL, document date where known, precise locator, access date, hash when downloaded and read-status limitations. The claim/evidence register separates reported fact, management statement, analyst calculation and hypothetical assumption. Safe numerical extracts and deterministic model code reproduce the complete canonical object; raw issuer PDFs, OCR/source text/images and individual/account identifiers are excluded from private backup archives. This limits the backup to analytical work and provenance, not an unredacted source collection.

Key open questions: final company-law outcome; actual October cash/debt and deposit encumbrance; updated IPO use and maturity classification; FY25 CFO/interim reclassification; capital-advance cash/balance difference; current facility terms and repayment fees; land final cost/payment; commissioning/accepted orders; project-level cash returns; September encumbrances/capital changes; and primary trading depth/circuit data. The model assumes 25% cash tax, 10% interest, depreciation at 10% of opening operating fixed capital, no dividends/new debt, explicit declining principal, scenario margins/growth/WC and exit multiples. These are transparent sensitivities, not company guidance. Fixed-capital depreciation and terminal ROIC need refinement as new commissioned-cohort evidence arrives. Financial-model precision does not remove evidence uncertainty.
